definitions.explanation: Letting someone or something take its own course without intervening or controlling. Often implies a deliberate hands-off approach.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{放任|ほうにん}する。
examples.english: To leave children to their own devices.

examples.japanese: {放任|ほうにん}{主義|しゅぎ}の{教育|きょういく}にはメリットもデメリットもある。
examples.english: A laissez-faire approach to education has both merits and demerits.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}を{放任|ほうにん}していたら、{取|と}り{返|かえ}しのつかないことになる。
examples.english: If you leave the problem alone, it will become irreversible.

notes: Common collocations: {放任|ほうにん}{主義|しゅぎ} (laissez-faire policy/approach), {放任|ほうにん}{教育|きょういく} (permissive/hands-off education). Often carries a negative nuance of neglect when used about parenting or responsibilities, but can be neutral or positive when describing economic or management philosophy.
